markdown-it's source is written as ES modules with the .mjs extension: all 53 modules under src/ (src/index.mjs, src/markdownit.mjs, src/parser_*.mjs, src/renderer.mjs, src/ruler.mjs, src/token.mjs and everything in src/common/, src/helpers/, src/presets/, src/rules_block/, src/rules_core/ and src/rules_inline/). Rename every one of them to the same path with the .ts extension (src/index.mjs to src/index.ts, src/rules_block/list.mjs to src/rules_block/list.ts, and so on), as the first step of moving the source to TypeScript, with behaviour unchanged. Node 24 runs .ts files directly by stripping types, so the renamed files stay plain JavaScript: do not add type annotations or change the code, and keep each file's content as it is apart from the module paths it imports (comments that link to a source file may follow the rename). Move each file so that no module remains under its old name and no .mjs file is left under src/, and do not leave files under the old names (no re-exporting stubs). Update every reference to an old path: the imports between modules in src/, the static and dynamic imports in the tests under test/, the bundle entries in support/build-dist.mjs, and the other scripts under support/ and benchmark/ that import the sources. Behaviour must not change: each renamed module exports exactly what it exported before; importing src/index.ts gives the same markdownit factory and the same output for every input and option set; Node prints no warning when the renamed sources load that it does not print for the current .mjs files (for example a warning about the module type of a .ts file); npm run build still produces dist/markdown-it.mjs, dist/markdown-it.cjs.js and the browser bundles with the same behaviour; and the command-line tool bin/markdown-it.mjs, which uses the built package, prints the same HTML. Adding a TypeScript configuration or a type-check script is not required. The tests are node:test files under test/, and the project's tests run with npm test (eslint, the build, then node --test over test/cmspec, test/markdown-it and test/build), which must keep passing.
